message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: Discarding both Lava Darts loses significant value. Lava Dart has flashback by sacrificing a Mountain, meaning each copy in the graveyard represents a free spell that triggers prowess/Slickshot Show-Off and can deal 1 damage. However, having two in the graveyard is partially redundant since you can only flash back one at a time (each requires sacrificing a Mountain). Keeping one Lava Dart in hand to cast normally (triggering prowess) and discarding one to the graveyard for flashback later would have been better. The other discard should be something like Violent Urge (situational without delirium) or one of the duplicate Preordains.

Playing Flooded Strand onto the battlefield means it gets locked under Blood Moon (which can be cast this turn) as just a Mountain, wasting its unique ability to fetch Islands/Plains. The Arid Mesa in hand similarly becomes dead under Blood Moon, but Flooded Strand's Island-fetching ability is more unique and valuable to preserve in hand for when Blood Moon might be removed.

message: Select a Plains or Island card
annotation_description: The player has Blood Moon in hand and plans to cast it this turn (it costs 2R). They already have Arena of Glory (which can produce R or RR if exerted) and are fetching with Arid Mesa. With Blood Moon in hand, fetching a basic Plains would be better because once Blood Moon resolves, all nonbasic lands become Mountains anyway - so Sacred Foundry's dual typing is irrelevant. Meanwhile, fetching Sacred Foundry costs 2 life (on top of the 1 life from Arid Mesa) for no benefit since Blood Moon will make it just a Mountain anyway. A basic Plains would save 2 life and still function as a Mountain under Blood Moon. However, fetching Sacred Foundry does let them cast Blood Moon this turn (Arena of Glory for R + Sacred Foundry for R + either source for the third R via exerting Arena), whereas a basic Plains only produces W without Blood Moon. Actually, let me reconsider: they need {2}{R} for Blood Moon. Arena of Glory taps for {R}, and if they fetch Sacred Foundry (untapped for 2 life), it taps for {R}. That's only 2 mana - not enough for Blood Moon this turn with just 2 lands. They could exert Arena of Glory to get {R}{R} (costs {R} to activate, so net +{R}{R} from Arena) plus Sacred Foundry for {R} = {R}{R}{R}, but exerting costs {R} which they don't have before tapping. Wait - exert cost is {R}, {T}: Add {R}{R}. So they need {R} to activate the exert ability, which they don't have from another source. So normal tap of Arena = {R}, Sacred Foundry = {R}, that's only 2 mana total. They can't cast Blood Moon this turn regardless. Given they can't cast Blood Moon this turn anyway, fetching a basic Plains would preserve the option of casting Guide of Souls ({W}) next turn while saving 2 life, and Blood Moon could come down turn 4. Sacred Foundry is slightly worse since it costs 2 extra life for marginal benefit.

With Blood Moon in hand and 3 mana available (Arena of Glory, Arid Mesa, Sacred Foundry), casting Blood Moon on turn 3 would be a strong tempo play that could lock the opponent out of non-red mana. The opponent likely has nonbasic lands that would become Mountains. Guide of Souls is a 1-drop that could be cast on a later turn alongside other spells, whereas Blood Moon is most impactful when cast early. Additionally, casting Guide of Souls before combat when holding no other creatures to trigger it immediately provides no value this turn, and it's vulnerable to the opponent's burn spells (Lava Dart flashback is available from the graveyard).

Casting Galvanic Discharge during combat when the opponent has no creatures or planeswalkers on the battlefield wastes a premium removal spell. The energy counters gained are minimal value compared to having the removal available for future threats like Monastery Swiftspear or Slickshot Show-Off.

Discarding Monastery Swiftspear (a key 1-mana threat with haste and prowess) instead of a redundant cantrip. In an Izzet Prowess deck, threats are more valuable than the 4th cantrip. Having both Swiftspear and Slickshot Show-Off provides more threat diversity and the ability to deploy multiple threats.

GLM47 Coach cast Galvanic Discharge targeting their OWN Guide of Souls, destroying one of their best creatures for no reason. Guide of Souls is a key piece of their strategy, providing life gain, energy counters, and the ability to buff attacking creatures. Using a removal spell on your own creature is a massive waste of resources - losing both the creature and the removal spell.

With only one land (Fiery Islet) on the battlefield on turn 5, the player is already severely mana-screwed. Sacrificing their only land to draw a card leaves them with zero lands in play. They have 7 cards in hand including Preordain (which costs U), Expressive Iteration (which costs UR), and Slickshot Show-Off (which costs 1R) — none of which can be cast without any lands. Casting Preordain with Fiery Islet's mana would let them scry 2 and draw, helping find lands while keeping their one land in play. Sacrificing the land means even if they draw a land next turn, they'll only have one land and be even further behind.

With only one land (Fiery Islet) and 8 cards in hand, MiniMx Analyst should cast Preordain first to dig for a land drop. Casting Monastery Swiftspear before Preordain means the Swiftspear won't get a prowess trigger from Preordain if cast afterward (well, it will get prowess from subsequent spells, but that's not the issue). The real problem is sequencing: Preordain lets you scry 2 and draw, potentially finding a second land to play this turn. If you cast Swiftspear first, you've used your only mana and can't cast Preordain. Actually wait - Fiery Islet only produces one mana, so they can only cast one spell this turn regardless. But Preordain would help find a land for next turn and set up future draws, while Swiftspear with no second land means very limited ability to chain spells and leverage prowess. However, having Swiftspear on board means next turn you can cast multiple cheap spells with prowess triggers. The bigger issue is that with only 1 land and needing to find more lands desperately, Preordain is likely better here to smooth draws. Swiftspear without mana to back it up is vulnerable and not impactful.

GLM47 Coach played Plains instead of considering deploying Blood Moon, which would be devastating against MiniMx Analyst's nonbasic land base (Fiery Islet becomes a Mountain). More importantly, playing Plains before deciding on the turn's plan is suboptimal sequencing. With 3 lands already in play (Arena of Glory, Arid Mesa, Sacred Foundry) and Plains as the 4th, the coach has access to 4 mana. However, the key issue is that playing Plains uses the land drop when Arid Mesa could have been cracked first to find a land, preserving the Plains in hand for a future turn. Additionally, casting Blood Moon (2R) was available this turn using Sacred Foundry + Arena of Glory + cracking Arid Mesa for a Mountain, which would turn the opponent's Fiery Islet into a basic Mountain and significantly limit their mana options. Playing Plains doesn't advance the Blood Moon plan as efficiently - though Blood Moon is still castable with Sacred Foundry (R) + Arena of Glory (R, exerted for RR) = RRR, which covers 2R. But playing Plains first and then Blood Moon means the Plains becomes a Mountain under Blood Moon. The better line was likely to cast Blood Moon this turn using existing mana sources before playing the land drop, preserving Plains for after Blood Moon resolves (where it would remain a Plains as a basic land).

Blood Moon is strong here since the opponent only has Fiery Islet (which becomes a Mountain), but GLM47 Coach has 4 lands including Arid Mesa which will also become a Mountain under Blood Moon. The issue is that casting Blood Moon before cracking Arid Mesa means Arid Mesa becomes a Mountain and can no longer be sacrificed to fetch. GLM47 Coach should have cracked Arid Mesa first to get a basic land (likely a Plains for white mana access), then cast Blood Moon. With Blood Moon in play, the Sacred Foundry and Arena of Glory both become Mountains, so GLM47 Coach loses access to white mana entirely unless they fetch a Plains first. This locks out Guide of Souls, Voice of Victory, and other white cards in hand.

Ragavan is a must-kill threat that will generate Treasure tokens and card advantage every combat. Under Blood Moon, MiniMx's Fiery Islet only produces red mana anyway, and most of their hand (Expressive Iteration, Preordain) requires blue mana they can't produce. Sacrificing the Mountain-ified Fiery Islet to flashback Lava Dart kills Ragavan at relatively low cost given the board state.

With delirium active (artifact, instant, creature, sorcery in graveyard), Violent Urge on the attacking Monastery Swiftspear would give +1/+0, first strike, AND double strike. Combined with prowess (+1/+1), Swiftspear would be a 3/3 double striker dealing 6 damage instead of just 1. Against an opponent at 16 life with Blood Moon constraining both players' mana, 5 extra damage is enormous.

Deployed Dragon's Rage Channeler instead of using Unholy Heat to kill Ragavan while delirium is active (4 card types in graveyard: artifact, instant, creature, sorcery). Ragavan on an untap will threaten combat damage generating treasure and card advantage. DRC can block Ragavan, but opponent has resources to potentially remove it.

Casting Violent Urge on Monastery Swiftspear in precombat main phase with no combat context wastes the spell. Violent Urge gives +1/+0 and first strike (or double strike with delirium) until end of turn - this is a combat trick that should be cast during combat to maximize damage or in response to removal. Casting it now triggers prowess on Swiftspear and DRC's surveil, but the card is much more valuable as a combat trick. Additionally, Blood Moon is on the battlefield turning all nonbasic lands into Mountains, meaning Fiery Islet is a Mountain. MiniMx has delirium check: graveyard has Mishra's Bauble (artifact), Lava Dart (instant), Monastery Swiftspear (creature), Preordain (sorcery) - that's 4 types, so delirium is active and Violent Urge would grant double strike. This makes it even more valuable to save for combat when you can use it on an attacking creature for maximum damage. However, the bigger issue is that casting it precombat means the opponent sees it and can make blocking decisions accordingly, whereas casting during combat after blocks would be much stronger.

GLM47 Coach declined to attack with Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer when both of the opponent's creatures (Monastery Swiftspear and Dragon's Rage Channeler) were tapped. This means there were zero blockers available, making the attack completely free. Attacking would deal 2 damage, create a Treasure token (useful for casting the Seasoned Pyromancer or Voice of Victory in hand), and exile the top card of the opponent's library for potential use.
